doc: Fleet default router (lanes-golive). Copy to <workspace>/.lanes/router.json and edit there. Rules are evaluated in order, first match wins; predicates are a fixed vocabulary read by lanes.ts (no model call). Nothing matched → main. Before any rule the router gives the fleet's wake-up lines their fixed destination (lanes.ts routeWake, from the event's `wake` field): keep-warm, STALL-WAKE, RESTART-WAKE and the resume line → the main; the 讀信箱 reminder → the mail lane, whose work queue is the agent's mailbox (mail, board notices, mail-tier alerts). Joey's Telegram → the main. Scheduler runs, page-tier alerts and peer calls → a reflex lane. A board work order pushed as a call (an urgent ticket) → a worker lane in Joey's DM topic (the main when topics are off). Mesh no_reply notices → the ledger (the main's next digest). What reaches Joey: every lane line rings (ORG-CHART §0 #2: 做了什麼就報什麼、全進 Joey 手機); a routine run with nothing new is one line (#5); a high-frequency run with nothing new is its receipt only (#5, the router opens no Joey line for it).

notify.doc: ORG-CHART §0 #2 and #5 (current rules): nothing that reaches Joey is silent. Every class pushes, plain or escalated; no frequency cap. The only line that does not go out is a no_reply notice (the ledger: it owed nobody a reply before lanes either) and a high-frequency routine with nothing new (no Joey line is opened for it: the receipt only). The notify profile `default` (LANES_NOTIFY_PROFILE, the fleet default) pushes everything whatever this table says; this table is what `/lanes notify tiered` would use, and it is the same.
